snippet.title: Can Antibiotics Affect Your Mental Health?
snippet.description:
🧠🦠 Can your gut health affect your mental health? In this fascinating discussion, Dr. Zach Bush explores the connection between **antibiotics, gut microbiome health, gut-brain communication, inflammation, depression, anxiety, mental health, and overall wellness**.

This conversation dives into topics surrounding **gut bacteria, microbiome diversity, antibiotics and health, digestive health, mood regulation, brain health, chronic inflammation, blood-brain barrier function, neurotransmitters, gut-brain axis, immune system health, microbiota, and long-term wellness**. ⚡🌱

As more research explores **gut health, microbiome science, mental health awareness, depression, anxiety, inflammation, nutrition, preventative health, biohacking, functional medicine, and health optimization**, many people are becoming interested in how **lifestyle choices, diet, sleep, stress, and the microbiome** may influence health outcomes.

💡 Your gut and brain may be more connected than most people realize.

⚠️ This content is for educational and discussion purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Scientific understanding of the microbiome and mental health continues to evolve.

snippet.title: Why Is America Getting Sicker?
snippet.description:
Agriculture policy, pesticide use, and food system structure are increasingly debated topics in nutrition and public health discussions. In this clip from Realfoodology, Courtney Swan discusses concerns around pesticide use in agriculture, crop subsidies, glyphosate exposure, and broader questions about chronic disease trends, food quality, and regulatory oversight.

The conversation covers glyphosate, herbicide use, pesticide-sprayed crops, agricultural subsidies, food supply chains, chronic disease, obesity rates, environmental exposure pathways (including water and food residues), and the ongoing debate about food system transparency and corporate influence in agriculture and food production.

This discussion reflects a broader public debate around food policy, health outcomes, and agricultural practices, including questions about how food is produced, regulated, and distributed.

snippet.title: The Most Dangerous Walk You'll Ever Take (& Why It's Worth It)
snippet.description:
Most people overlook this simple walking exercise that supports ankle strength, hamstring flexibility, and helps improve balance naturally. Discover the profound benefits of reverse walking for brain health, knee pain relief, mobility, and more. It can even promote brain rewiring!

0:00 Introduction: Walking for brain health
0:59 Natural movement/walking on flat surfaces 
3:00 Walking backwards 
3:14 Backward walking benefits
3:52 Walking backwards uphill
4:57 How to prevent injury while reverse walking

The Backward Hill Protocol: https://drbrg.co/4xCZ1Ki

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4vFlip4

Keep watching for more powerful ways to improve movement and support longevity:
https://youtu.be/zs1a8tFsvdc
https://youtu.be/JQo_edypQOE
https://youtu.be/HXt5kTTTrho

Read more on natural ways to reduce pain and inflammation here: https://drbrg.co/4uOlNwG

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Walking on flat surfaces does not mimic natural movement. Natural movement involves uneven terrain, inclines, rocks, and other unpredictable surfaces that challenge the body and brain.

The cerebellum, which controls balance, contains nearly half of the brain's neurons. When movement becomes repetitive and automatic, the brain doesn’t have to work as hard. Novel movement and changing pressure patterns can help stimulate the brain in new ways.

Reverse walking shifts pressure away from the knees and forces the hamstrings and glutes to become more active.

Some of the benefits of reverse walking include:
• Reduced knee pressure
• Improved hamstring flexibility
• Better balance and coordination
• Cognitive function improvement

Once you’re comfortable with reverse walking, try walking backwards uphill. Reverse walking uphill is one of the best glute activation exercises and can also help improve ankle strength and coordination.

snippet.description:
Looking for tinnitus relief? Discover the root cause of ringing in the ears, how tinnitus may be connected to metabolic health, and what you can do to support ear health naturally in as little as 7 days.

0:00 How to stop ringing in ears

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Ringing in the ears is often associated with past exposure to loud noise, but there may be additional factors involved.

Tinnitus is believed to originate in the brain rather than the ears themselves. When hearing loss occurs at a specific frequency, the brain may generate a sound to compensate for the missing signal.

Chronically elevated blood sugar can affect the tiny nerves and blood vessels of the inner ear. Many people have blood sugar problems for years without realizing it because insulin levels can rise long before blood sugar levels become noticeably abnormal.

Supporting healthy blood sugar levels may play an important role in tinnitus relief. Reducing carbohydrate intake and incorporating fasting may help support healthy insulin levels and improve nutrient delivery to the small blood vessels that support hearing.

These two nutrients help support nerve health and cardiovascular function for natural tinnitus relief:
1. Alpha-lipoic acid
2. Benfotiamine

Some people report improvements relatively quickly, while others may require more time depending on the underlying factors involved.
